beats.role_note: Q1 what it is, one sentence (BRIEF §1). Real play at a7, scripted input: the jab landing.
beats.narration_text: I'm Tharun Maheswararao. My final project is the Tin Knockout Fighter Kit: a fighter controller and animation state machine for Godot four, where every move is written in frames and pinned by tests a stranger can rerun. This is my game at tag a seven, from scripted input.

beats.role_note: Q2 result of B02: the jab whiff, the jab landing with hitstop, and the cutlass (K), real play at a7, scripted input; readout from the capture log. Clock gap: TEST-REPORT A7-9e.
beats.narration_text: In play: the jab's box opens on its fifth tick. When it lands, hitstop holds both fighters, and the animation holds with them, because each clip is put at the state timer every tick. On my Apple M four, that gap measured zero seconds. Press K, and the cutlass lands nine ticks in.

beats.role_note: Q4 different (BRIEF §4): Street Fighter 6 and Tekken 8 named in text only (games Tharun has played); no footage or art from them.
beats.narration_text: I've played Street Fighter six and Tekken eight. They're far larger, finished games, and this doesn't compete with them. Their frame data is something a player reads. Here, a programmer can open the state machine that makes the frames, and rerun the tests that prove them.

beats.role_note: Q4 its own mechanic (BRIEF §4): the wind-up spring. Real play at a7, scripted input: Bolt holds S, the key turns, wind climbs.
beats.narration_text: And Tin Knockout has its own mechanic: a wind-up spring that every move drains. You rewind it by holding S, and you're open while you crank.

beats.role_note: Q5 who opens it and the first sixty seconds (BRIEF §5). Steps 1-4 are WILL; the second path is real recorded output today.
beats.narration_text: My target role is gameplay programmer. The reader is a lead engineer or hiring manager, with sixty seconds. They'll double-click the build, land in the training room with no menu, press J to see the jab counted, then K for the cutlass's different timing. Today, one command already prints seventy checks, zero failed.

beats.role_note: Q6 what it proves (BRIEF §6), each with its tag and TEST-REPORT record.
beats.narration_text: What does it prove? Animation and state: one authority per animated node, clips synced to the state timer. Verification: pins before and after a change, edge tests at every boundary, mutations in git worktrees, and a seam bug a fixture log caught after the suite passed it. Profiling: two clocks, measured on the M four. And shaders and particles that read the fighter, and never write it.

beats.narration_text: Out: netcode, a second character's art, more arenas, saving. In: the reusable scene; an animated cutlass, block and hurt; an input buffer; the overlay; the training room; and the mac export. First, the fighter will run as its own scene against a still dummy, and the three a seven suites will give the same counts against it.

beats.role_note: Q7 the risk (BRIEF §7): main.gd drives the fighter. main.gd:180-182 at a7; lines 61 and 80-81 as source notes.
beats.narration_text: What could sink it? Today, main dot G D drives the fighter: line one eighty-one calls its step, and main also sets its opponent and its cork spawner. Untangling that could silently move a frame boundary.

beats.role_note: Result of B11: the mitigation. test_a7_pins.gd (which runs main.tscn) re-run at 60 and 30 on a0c95cc, recorded output; plus the renderer risk (BRIEF §7).
beats.narration_text: So the pins come first: they lock every boundary at sixty and at thirty frames a second, and the refactor won't be committed unless they pass with identical logs. And since the game renders with Forward plus on Vulkan, the Mac build will be tested on the M four before I claim anything. No web build.

beats.role_note: Q8 why this project (BRIEF §8): a mix, with tags for the existing skills.
beats.narration_text: Why this project? A mix. I already have shaders, particles and a pinned state machine, and I've directed an agent with scoped plans. New to me: a reusable scene, an input buffer, an overlay, and a desktop export with a measured frame rate. And I'll test whether an AnimationTree helps by building the cutlass both ways.
